ai.description: This 25–30 mm frog is yellowish-brown with a distinct dark brown hourglass pattern on its back. It features a pointed snout and granular skin, lacking webbing between its toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Amboli Bush Frog is best distinguished by the distinct, bright yellow or orange webbing between its toes, which is absent in most other similar *Pseudophilautus* species.
ai.habitat: The Amboli bush frog inhabits the evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found on low-lying vegetation at altitudes between 600 and 800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Amboli bush frog is strictly nocturnal, remaining hidden among dense foliage during the day and emerging at night to hunt for small insects in the forest understory.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Pseudophilautus amboli* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in terrestrial nests.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Amboli bush frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically inhabiting the states of Maharashtra and Karnataka at elevations between 600 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Amboli Bush Frog produces a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink-tink" notes, typically heard emanating from dense vegetation in its humid forest habitat.
